newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope appears at Vatican, appeals for Ugandans.
newsitem.headline: Pope appears at Vatican, appeals for Ugandans.

text.p: Pope John Paul, addressing the faithful at the Vatican for the first time since he underwent surgery earlier this month, on Sunday thanked wellwishers and said he was touched by their concern.

The Pope, speaking from the balcony of his apartments overlooking the square outside St Peter's Basilica, also made a strong appeal for the release of a group of female Catholic students reported kidnapped in Uganda.
After devoting his regular noon Angelus address to World Missionary Day, celebrated on Sunday, the Pontiff said the day had been overshadowed by news from Uganda.
He said a group of Catholic women students had been kidnapped in Aboke, in the north of the country. News reports said the girls were abducted earlier this month.
"Thirty girls are still in the hands of their kidnappers, while their families and the Catholic Community are suffering hours of anguish over their fate," the Pope said.

"I appeal to the consciences of those responsible so that this brutal abduction can be ended: Respect the lives and dignity of these youngsters. In the name of God I ask for their immediate liberation," the Pope continued.

The Pontiff also thanked those involved in missionary work and recalled the recent deaths of seven Trappist monks and the bishop of Oran in Algeria as well as the killing of Burundian Archbishop Joachim Ruhuna.

The Pope, in remarks later to Polish pilgrims, repeated his attack on attempts to liberalise abortion laws in his native country, saying that "a nation that kills its own children is a nation with no future."
Earlier the Pope thanked the large crowd of pilgrims, some clutching coloured balloons as they waited in the sunshine for the Pope to appear, for their concern about his health.

"I am pleased to be able to say with you once again the Angelus prayers from this window from which I can contemplate the dome that Michelangelo's genius erected over the tomb of the apostle Peter," he told pilgrims in the square.
"Your presence confirms the love with which you followed me in recent days, giving me comfort and support."

The 76-year-old Polish born Pope had a successful operation to remove an appendix on October 8 and left Rome's Gemelli hospital last Tuesday. He gave his Angelus address from the window of his 10th floor hospital suite last Sunday.
The Pope, who has been ordered to rest as much as possible as he continues his convalescence, read the address in full on Sunday but made two long pauses and appeared tired.
He coughed audibly as he turned away from the window and his left hand trembled -- a problem that media reports have suggested is caused by Parkinson's disease.
The Vatican has yet to set a date for the Pope resuming his regular activities.
